questions.question: What was the theme of the World Sustainable Development Summit 2025?

options.text: Partnerships for Accessing Supportive Development and Climate Solutions
Partnership for Accessing Sustainable Development and Climate Solutions
Partnership for Accelerating Sustainable Development and Climate Solutions
Partnership for Approaching Sustainable Development and Climate Change

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Partnership for Accelerating Sustainable Development and Climate Solutions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The theme of the **World Sustainable Development Summit (WSDS) 2025** is "**Partnership for Accelerating Sustainable Development and Climate Solutions**."
 
• The WSDS is an annual flagship event organized by **The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI)**, headquartered in **New Delhi, India**.
 
• This theme highlights the importance of **global partnerships** to address challenges like **climate change** and achieve the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• The summit serves as a platform for **policy-makers, researchers, and industry leaders** to collaborate and discuss actionable strategies for a sustainable future.
 
• It emphasizes **climate solutions** through **technological advancements, inclusive policies, and international cooperation**.
 
• By accelerating sustainable development, the summit aims to ensure a balance between **economic growth, environmental conservation, and social inclusion**.
 
• The WSDS is aligned with global frameworks such as the **Paris Agreement** and the **United Nations 2030 Agenda**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Partnerships for Accessing Supportive Development and Climate Solutions**__

 __
 
• This option incorrectly mentions "Accessing Supportive Development," which is not the focus of the summit's theme.
 
• The correct emphasis is on **accelerating solutions** rather than just accessing support.
 
 
 
• **Partnership for Accessing Sustainable Development and Climate Solutions**__
 __
 
• This option incorrectly uses the term "Accessing Sustainable Development."
 
• The summit theme focuses on **speeding up (accelerating) development** rather than merely accessing it.
 
 
 
• **Partnership for Approaching Sustainable Development and Climate Change**__
 
 
• This option incorrectly uses the term "Approaching," which does not align with the dynamic and urgent nature of the summit's objectives.
 
• The focus is on **action and acceleration**, not just approaching the issues.

questions.question: When was the discovery of salvarsan recognised with a Nobel Prize in Medicine?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1908**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The discovery of **Salvarsan (arsphenamine)**, the first effective treatment for syphilis, was made by **Paul Ehrlich and his team** in 1907.
 
• Paul Ehrlich was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1908**, shared with Ilya Mechnikov, for their work on immunity.
 
• The Nobel Prize recognized Ehrlich's groundbreaking contributions, including the development of Salvarsan and his "magic bullet" concept for targeted therapies.
 
• Salvarsan is considered a significant milestone in the history of chemotherapy and the treatment of infectious diseases.
 
• The discovery marked the beginning of the use of synthetic drugs to combat microbial infections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salvarsan (Arsphenamine):**

 
 
• It was the first synthetic antimicrobial drug used to treat syphilis, a bacterial infection caused by Treponema pallidum.
 
• The drug belongs to the arsenic compound class and was a precursor to modern antibiotics.
 
• Salvarsan was introduced into medical practice in 1910 and was considered revolutionary for its time.
 
 
 
• **Paul Ehrlich:**
 
 
• A German physician and scientist known as the "Father of Chemotherapy."
 
• He developed the "magic bullet" theory, envisioning drugs that could specifically target disease-causing organisms without harming the host.
 
• His work laid the foundation for modern pharmacology and immunology.
 
 
 
• **Nobel Prize in 1908:**
 
 
• The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1908 was awarded jointly to Paul Ehrlich and Ilya Mechnikov.
 
• Ilya Mechnikov's contribution involved the discovery of phagocytosis, a key mechanism of innate immunity.
 
• Their combined work advanced the understanding of immunological responses and therapeutic interventions.
 
 
 
• **Syphilis:**
 
 
• A sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum.
 
• Symptoms include sores, rashes, and, in severe cases, damage to organs and the nervous system.
 
• Before Salvarsan, syphilis was treated with mercury compounds, which were highly toxic and ineffective.

questions.question: Which of the following could be the factors that led Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to withdraw significant funds from Indian equities according to the Economic Survey 2024-25? 1. Slowing earnings growth 2. High valuations 3. Rising geopolitical tensions
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All 1, 2, and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Economic Survey 2024-25** highlights multiple factors that could have influenced the withdrawal of Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) from Indian equities.
 
• **Slowing earnings growth**: Reduced corporate earnings impact investor confidence, leading to lower equity investments.
 
• **High valuations**: Overvaluation of Indian stocks relative to other emerging markets or global benchmarks can deter FPIs.
 
• **Rising geopolitical tensions**: Escalating global or regional uncertainties (e.g., conflicts, trade wars) often make investors shift funds to safer markets.
 
• The combination of these factors heightens market risk and makes Indian equities less attractive compared to other investment destinations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foreign Portfolio Investments (FPIs):**

 
 
• FPIs include investments in stocks, bonds, or other financial assets in a foreign country without obtaining significant ownership.
 
• Such investments are more volatile and sensitive to economic, political, and market conditions.
 
 
 
• **High Valuations:**
 
 
• Stock valuations are often measured using indicators like the Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio.
 
• Overvaluation occurs when stock prices are excessively higher than their actual earnings potential.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Tensions:**
 
 
• These refer to conflicts or uncertainties between nations that may disrupt global trade, investments, and market stability.
 
• Examples include trade wars, sanctions, or military escalations.
 
 
 
• **Impact of FPI Outflows:**
 
 
• Significant withdrawal of FPIs can weaken the domestic currency due to reduced capital inflows.
 
• It can also lead to stock market volatility and reduced liquidity.
 
 
 
• **Economic Survey:**
 
 
• The Economic Survey is an annual document presented by the Indian Ministry of Finance before the Union Budget.
 
• It provides a detailed review of the economic developments in India during the past financial year.

questions.question: In 2024, the Indian government approved defence acquisitions worth $17.3 billion. How much percentage of these acquisitions was sourced from domestic suppliers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**99%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2024, the Indian government approved defence acquisitions worth $17.3 billion to strengthen national security and bolster defence capabilities.
 
• Out of the total approved acquisitions, only **99%** was sourced from domestic suppliers, reflecting a focus on international procurement for advanced technologies.
 
• This highlights the continued reliance on foreign suppliers for high-tech military equipment despite government initiatives to promote indigenous defence manufacturing.
 
• India has launched policies like **‘Make in India’** and Defence Production and Export Promotion Policy (DPEPP) to boost domestic production, but challenges in scaling technology remain.
 
• The low percentage underscores the need for further investment and development in domestic defence industries to reduce dependency on imports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Make in India Initiative**

 
 
• Launched in September 2014, it aims to transform India into a global manufacturing hub.
 
• Encourages investments in 25 sectors, including defence manufacturing.
 
• Focuses on reducing imports and increasing domestic production capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Defence Production and Export Promotion Policy (DPEPP) 2020**
 
 
• Aims to achieve a turnover of Rs. 1,75,000 crore ($25 billion) in defence manufacturing by 2025.
 
• Focuses on increasing exports to Rs. 35,000 crore ($5 billion) by 2025.
 
• Promotes self-reliance in defence production by encouraging private sector participation.
 
 
 
• **Offset Policy in Defence Procurement**
 
 
• Introduced to leverage foreign defence procurement for domestic capabilities.
 
• Mandates foreign suppliers to invest a percentage of the contract value in Indian industries.
 
• Helps promote technology transfer and industrial collaboration.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Indigenous Defence Manufacturing**
 
 
• Limited access to advanced technologies and research capabilities.
 
• High dependence on foreign collaborations for critical components.
 
• Need for policy reforms to streamline procurement and production processes.

questions.question: In which year was the Smart Cities Mission launched to enhance the quality of life in 100 selected cities by providing efficient services, robust infrastructure, and a sustainable environment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Smart Cities Mission** was launched by the Government of India on **25th June 2015**.
 
• This mission aims to enhance the quality of life in **100 selected cities** by providing efficient services, robust infrastructure, and a sustainable environment.
 
• The initiative emphasizes **smart solutions** for urban challenges, such as better water and electricity supply, sanitation, and waste management.
 
• The focus is on creating **citizen-friendly and sustainable urban spaces** through the use of technology and innovation.
 
• The mission is implemented by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs** under the Government of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smart Cities Mission Overview:**

 
 
• Under the mission, cities are developed with **core infrastructure**, including adequate water supply, assured electricity, sanitation, affordable housing, and mobility.
 
• Smart Cities aim to use **data-driven decision-making** for efficient resource management.
 
• Implementation is done through the **Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)** created at the city level.
 
 
 
• **Funding Structure:**
 
 
• The mission operates on a **public-private partnership (PPP) model** to attract investments.
 
• The central government provides financial support of **₹48,000 crore** over five years, with matching contributions from state governments.
 
 
 
• **Selection of Cities:**
 
 
• Cities were selected through a **competitive process** known as the Smart City Challenge.
 
• The selection criteria included **economic growth potential, citizen engagement, and feasibility of smart solutions.**
 
 
 
• **Examples of Smart Initiatives:**
 
 
• Use of **IoT (Internet of Things)** for traffic management and surveillance.
 
• Smart metering for utilities like water and electricity.
 
• Development of **green spaces** and eco-friendly urban projects.

questions.question: Which of the following changes did the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 make?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Added Muslim women to boards**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 mandated the inclusion of **Muslim women** as members of State Waqf Boards to ensure gender representation and inclusivity.
 
• This amendment aimed to provide a platform for Muslim women to actively participate in the governance and management of Waqf properties.
 
• By including women, the amendment sought to address long-standing issues of gender disparity in decision-making roles within the Waqf Boards.
 
• The inclusion of Muslim women aligns with broader national and global efforts to promote gender equality in governance structures.
 
• The move was widely welcomed as a progressive step towards empowering Muslim women in community affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Waqf:**

 
 
• A waqf is an endowment made by a Muslim for religious, educational, or charitable purposes.
 
• Waqf properties are typically donated in perpetuity, and their income is used for the intended purpose.
 
• The management of Waqf properties is overseen by Waqf Boards established in each state under the Waqf Act, 1995.
 
 
 
• **Waqf Boards:**
 
 
• State Waqf Boards are statutory bodies responsible for administering Waqf properties in their respective states.
 
• The members of the board are appointed as per the provisions of the Waqf Act, which includes representation from various stakeholders.
 
 
 
• **Role of Women in Governance:**
 
 
• Inclusion of women in governance structures fosters diversity and better representation of community needs.
 
• Research shows that gender-balanced boards tend to have better decision-making processes and outcomes.
 
 
 
• **Other Amendments in the Waqf Act:**
 
 
• The Waqf Act has been amended multiple times to address issues such as transparency, dispute resolution, and better management of Waqf properties.
 
• Each amendment reflects efforts to modernize and make the administration of Waqf properties more efficient.

questions.question: In January 2025, for the first time, the Government of India has decided to provide financial assistance to the Indian contingent participating in the 9th Asian Winter Games 2025 under which of the following schemes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assistance to National Sports Federations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "Assistance to National Sports Federations" scheme is a key initiative of the Government of India to promote sports through financial support to recognized federations.
 
• This scheme provides financial assistance for training, equipment purchase, participation in international events, and hosting national-level tournaments.
 
• The scheme is instrumental in enhancing the performance of Indian athletes in international competitions, including multi-sport events like the Asian Winter Games.
 
• Under this scheme, federations are encouraged to develop sports infrastructure and provide better coaching facilities to athletes.
 
• The financial assistance also covers expenses for exposure trips, enabling athletes to train and compete globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khelo India Scheme:**

 
 
• A flagship program launched in 2018 to promote a culture of sports and fitness in India.
 
• The scheme emphasizes building sports infrastructure, organizing talent hunts, and providing scholarships to young athletes.
 
• Khelo India Youth Games and University Games are major events under this initiative.
 
 
 
• **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS):**
 
 
• Launched in 2014, this scheme aims to identify and support elite athletes with the potential to win Olympic medals.
 
• TOPS provides financial support for training, equipment, coaching, and international exposure.
 
• It focuses on disciplines with high medal prospects, ensuring specialized attention to top athletes.
 
 
 
• **Fit India Movement:**
 
 
• A nationwide campaign launched in 2019 to promote physical fitness and a healthy lifestyle.
 
• It emphasizes awareness programs, fitness challenges, and collaboration with schools and workplaces.
 
 
 
• **Asian Winter Games:**
 
 
• A multi-sport event organized by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) for winter sports.
 
• The 9th edition is scheduled for 2025, providing a platform for athletes from Asian countries to compete in winter disciplines.
 
• India's participation is significant for promoting winter sports in the country.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund (UIDF) announced in the Union Budget 2023-24?

options.text: To utilise priority sector lending shortfall

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To utilise priority sector lending shortfall**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Urban Infrastructure Development Fund (UIDF) was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24 to **address the infrastructure needs of Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities**.
 
• It is **financed through the shortfall in priority sector lending**, which banks are mandated to fulfill.
 
• The fund aims to enhance urban infrastructure, including **modernizing roads, public transport, waste management systems, and other civic services**.
 
• The National Housing Bank (NHB) will **manage and oversee the implementation** of UIDF.
 
• This initiative promotes **sustainable urban development**, ensuring that smaller cities also benefit from enhanced infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Priority Sector Lending (PSL):**

 
 
• PSL mandates banks to allocate a specific portion of their lending to sectors like agriculture, MSMEs, and affordable housing.
 
• In case of shortfall, banks contribute to funds like RIDF (Rural Infrastructure Development Fund) or UIDF.
 
 
 
• **Tier 2 and Tier 3 Cities:**
 
 
• These cities are classified based on population size, with Tier 2 cities having populations between 50,000 and 1,00,000, and Tier 3 cities between 20,000 and 50,000.
 
• Such cities often lack sufficient infrastructure and require targeted development efforts.
 
 
 
• **National Housing Bank (NHB):**
 
 
• It is the apex financial institution for housing in India, established in 1988.
 
• NHB plays a pivotal role in implementing housing-related schemes and managing funds like UIDF.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Urban Development:**
 
 
• This concept emphasizes creating infrastructure that meets current needs without compromising resources for future generations.
 
• It includes green energy, efficient waste management, and smart city initiatives.

questions.question: What type of AI model did the Indian Institute of Science (IIS) team use in 2025 to generate synthetic images that help improve object detection?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diffusion Model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2025, the Indian Institute of Science (IIS) developed a synthetic image generation model using **Diffusion Models** to enhance object detection techniques.
 
• Diffusion Models are a class of generative AI models known for their capacity to produce high-quality synthetic data, including images.
 
• The IIS team applied the model to create diverse training datasets that addressed real-world challenges like class imbalance in object detection tasks.
 
• These models use a process of iteratively denoising data to reconstruct high-quality, realistic outputs.
 
• The implementation significantly improved the accuracy and robustness of AI-based object detection systems in various applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diffusion Models:**

 
 
• These are generative models that learn to reverse the process of gradually adding noise to data, reconstructing it into high-quality outputs.
 
• Introduced initially in the context of physics-based simulations, diffusion models have seen significant advancements in AI applications.
 
• They are particularly effective in generating realistic images, audio, and even text.
 
 
 
• **Generative AI Models:**
 
 
• Generative models aim to create new data instances that resemble existing data.
 
• Popular examples include Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), and Diffusion Models.
 
• These models are used in applications like content creation, data augmentation, and simulation environments.
 
 
 
• **Object Detection:**
 
 
• Object detection is a computer vision task focused on identifying and localizing objects within an image or video.
 
• It is widely used in areas like autonomous vehicles, surveillance, and medical imaging.
 
• Training robust object detection models requires diverse and balanced datasets.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Synthetic Data:**
 
 
• Synthetic data is artificially generated data that mimics real-world data characteristics.
 
• It is used to solve issues like data scarcity, privacy concerns, and class imbalance.
 
• Applications span across AI training, simulation, and testing environments.

questions.question: As of February 2025, how many athletes trained under Khelo India have set international records?

questions.question: Which cricket team won the 2024 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup held in the UAE, securing their first title in this format?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Zealand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• New Zealand’s women’s cricket team won the **2024 ICC Women's T20 World Cup**, marking their first-ever title in this format.
 
• The tournament was held in the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)** from February to March 2024.
 
• New Zealand defeated **England** in the final by showcasing exceptional performances in both batting and bowling.
 
• Prominent players like **Sophie Devine** and **Amelia Kerr** played pivotal roles in securing the victory.
 
• This win broke the dominance of traditional favorites like Australia and England in ICC Women's T20 World Cups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC Women's T20 World Cup:**

 
 
• The ICC Women's T20 World Cup is a biennial international championship for women's Twenty20 cricket organized by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
 
• The tournament was first held in **2009**, and Australia has been the most successful team, winning the title multiple times.
 
• It serves as a platform to promote women's cricket globally, showcasing talent and inspiring future generations.
 
 
 
• **Sophie Devine:**
 
 
• Sophie Devine is the captain of the New Zealand women’s cricket team and a renowned all-rounder known for her aggressive batting and impactful bowling.
 
• She holds several records, including the fastest century in Women’s T20 International cricket.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct with reference to the Supreme Court judgement in 'The State Of Tamil Nadu vs The Governor Of Tamil Nadu' on 8 April 2025?

1. The Supreme Court held that the Governor cannot withhold assent after a bill is re-passed by the legislature.

2. The Court used its powers under Article 142 to deem 10 pending Bills as having received assent.

3. The judgement laid down that the Governor may reserve a re-enacted Bill for Presidential consideration.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court ruled that the Governor does not have the discretion to withhold assent to a Bill once it is re-passed by the legislature, as per the constitutional framework.
 
• The Court exercised its powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to declare 10 pending Bills as having received the Governor's assent, ensuring legislative processes are not unduly delayed.
 
• The judgment emphasized that withholding assent by the Governor without valid reasons undermines the legislative authority of the elected assembly.
 
• The decision reinforces the principle of cooperative federalism and ensures accountability of constitutional functionaries like Governors.
 
• The judgment did not include any provision for the Governor to reserve a re-enacted Bill for Presidential consideration, focusing solely on legislative assent processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 142:** It grants the Supreme Court wide discretionary powers to pass decrees or orders to ensure "complete justice" in any case, even if such actions are not explicitly provided in the statute.
 
• **Role of the Governor:** As per the Indian Constitution, the Governor acts as the constitutional head of the state and is required to act on the advice of the state council of ministers in most matters.
 
• **Legislative Process:** Once a Bill is passed by a state legislature, it is sent to the Governor for assent. The Governor can assent, withhold, return (if not a money Bill), or reserve it for Presidential consideration.
 
• **Cooperative Federalism:** This principle emphasizes the collaboration between the Union and state governments while respecting each other's jurisdictions as outlined in the Constitution.
 
• **Judicial Review:** The judiciary has the power to review the actions of constitutional authorities, including Governors, to ensure they act within their constitutional limits.

questions.question: According to Airports Authority of India, which Indian airport was the busiest in terms of passenger traffic in Financial Year 2023-2024?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hansa NG (Next Generation) trainer aircraft has a range of **620 nautical miles**, making it suitable for training and short missions.
 
• It is an advanced version of the original Hansa aircraft, developed by the **National Aerospace Laboratories (NAL), Bengaluru.**
 
• The aircraft is designed for **pilot training, surveillance, and general aviation purposes.**
 
• Hansa NG features a **fuel-efficient engine**, lightweight design, and state-of-the-art avionics.
 
• The aircraft is expected to play a significant role in **boosting India's aviation training infrastructure** and promoting indigenously developed technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Aerospace Laboratories (NAL):**

 
 
• It is a premier aerospace research center in India under the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR).
 
• NAL focuses on development of civil aircraft, advanced technologies, and aerospace systems.
 
• Hansa NG is one of its flagship projects in the domain of general aviation.
 
 
 
• **Trainer Aircraft:**
 
 
• Trainer aircraft are specifically designed for pilot training.
 
• They feature dual controls, allowing instructors to assist trainees during flight.
 
• Hansa NG is considered ideal for basic flight training due to its compact size and efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Avionics:**
 
 
• Avionics refers to electronic systems used in aircraft for navigation, communication, and monitoring.
 
• Hansa NG is equipped with modern avionics to enhance pilot training and operational capabilities.
 
 
 
• **General Aviation:**
 
 
• General aviation covers all civilian flying activities outside of commercial airline operations.
 
• Hansa NG aims to strengthen India's general aviation sector by offering an indigenously developed solution.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Operation Brahma, launched in March 2025.

 
• The operation was launched by the Government of India to assist Myanmar and Thailand after a major earthquake.
 
• Indian Navy ships Satpura and Savitri from the Eastern Naval Command sailed for Yangon with relief material.
 
• The Indian Army deployed a 118-member medical task force from the Shatrujeet Brigade as part of the relief efforts.
 
• A 60-bed Medical Treatment Centre was set up by the Indian Army in Thailand for trauma and emergency care.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4 (Only 1, 2, and 3)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Operation Brahma** was launched in March 2025 by the Government of India to provide assistance to Myanmar and Thailand following a major earthquake.
 
• Indian Navy ships **Satpura** and **Savitri** from the Eastern Naval Command carried relief materials to Yangon, Myanmar.
 
• The Indian Army deployed a **118-member medical task force** from the Shatrujeet Brigade to support relief efforts in affected areas.
 
• The statement regarding a 60-bed Medical Treatment Centre being set up by the Indian Army in Thailand is not mentioned in the official records, making statement 4 incorrect.
 
• Thus, only statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Operation Brahma**:

 
 
• It is part of India’s Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) initiatives aimed at providing emergency support to neighboring countries during natural disasters.
 
• Such operations enhance India's role as a first responder in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR).
 
 
 
• **Indian Navy’s Role in Disaster Relief:**
 
 
• The Indian Navy often deploys ships carrying essential supplies, medical teams, and equipment to disaster-stricken areas.
 
• Past operations include Operation Samudra Maitri (Indonesia, 2018) and Operation Vanilla (Madagascar, 2020).
 
 
 
• **Shatrujeet Brigade:**
 
 
• An elite airborne brigade of the Indian Army specializing in rapid deployment and disaster relief operations.
 
• It has a proven track record of responding to emergencies and humanitarian needs in both domestic and international scenarios.
 
 
 
• **India’s Humanitarian Diplomacy:**
 
 
• India’s assistance during natural disasters strengthens bilateral relations and promotes regional stability.
 
• Such operations align with India’s “Neighborhood First” and “Act East” policies.
